query: What recurring issues drive resolution inefficiency?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Describes what kind of incident it is (subject matter), not an aspect of WHY resolution was inefficient. Category is context/predictor of inefficiency, not a constitutive part of the inefficiency reason itself.

per_column.name: failure_type
per_column.rationale: Characterises the nature of the underlying failure, i.e. the problem being solved, not a facet of the inefficiency of its resolution. It is an antecedent condition, not a part-of the inefficiency concept.

per_column.name: resolution_action_type
per_column.rationale: The type of resolution action (repair, investigation_only, etc.) is genuinely an aspect OF the resolution process whose (in)efficiency is under study, capturing a process facet of inefficiency.

per_column.name: reassignment_indicator
per_column.rationale: Reassignment/ping-pong is a canonical constitutive driver and aspect of resolution inefficiency (workflow churn facet).

per_column.name: self_resolution_indicator
per_column.rationale: Whether the incident self-resolved vs required active intervention is an aspect of the resolution process and its efficiency, a legitimate handling facet.

per_column.name: resolver_agent
per_column.rationale: Identity of the agent is a dimension/predictor associated with inefficiency, not a constitutive aspect OF the inefficiency reason. It is a grouping attribute, not a part-of the concept.

per_column.name: scope_breadth
per_column.rationale: The breadth/scope of impact is an aspect of the incident's handling complexity that constitutes an inefficiency-relevant facet (scale of what must be resolved).

per_column.name: affected_asset_class
per_column.rationale: The asset involved describes the subject of the incident, a predictor/context, not a constitutive aspect of why resolution was inefficient. It also largely overlaps with incident_category.

judge.rationale: Only about half the columns are true meronymic facets of 'inefficiency reasons'. incident_category, failure_type, resolver_agent, and affected_asset_class describe the incident's subject/context or grouping predictors rather than aspects OF the inefficiency itself. Mutual exclusivity is weakened by heavy overlap among incident_category, failure_type, and affected_asset_class (all essentially encode what/which asset), and even among the real facets, reassignment and self_resolution both touch handling flow. Exhaustiveness is low: the genuine facets omit key constitutive drivers of inefficiency such as delays/wait time, escalation/priority handling, information/diagnosis gaps, and rework, so the set does not cover the concept's main aspects.
